'''Tobias Bonhoeffer''' (born January 9, 1960) is a German-American [[neurobiologist]]. He is director of the department Synapses – Circuits – Plasticity and current managing director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biological Intelligence]] in [[Martinsried]] near [[Munich]] (formerly [[Max Planck Institute of Neurobiology]]).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://idw-online.de/en/news788973 |title=New Max Planck Institute for Biological Intelligence, in foundation |publisher=idw-online.de |access-date=2022-04-20}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Bonhoeffer was born on January 9, 1960 in [[Berkeley, California]], U.S., as his father [[Friedrich Bonhoeffer]] was doing postdoctoral research in the lab of [[Howard Schachman]] at the [[University_of_California,_Berkeley|University of 
California, Berkeley]] at the time. Shortly after his birth, the family returned to Germany, where his father took up a position at the Max Planck Institute for Virus Research in [[Tübingen]]. He later was appointed director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology]] in Tübingen.

== Education and career==
Bonhoeffer studied physics at the [[University of Tübingen]]. He received his doctorate at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics]] in Tübingen. As a postdoctoral fellow, he worked at [[Rockefeller University]] (USA) and at the [[Max Planck Institute for Brain Research]] in [[Frankfurt | Frankfurt am Main]]. He then headed an independent research group at the [[Max Planck Institute of Psychiatry]] in [[Munich]] and was appointed in 1998 director at the [[Max Planck Institute of Neurobiology]]—which merged with the [[Max Planck Institute for Ornithology]] to the new, joint [[Max Planck Institute for Biological Intelligence]] in 2023.

From 2008 until 2011, Tobias Bonhoeffer was chairman of the Biology & Medicine Section of the [[Max Planck Society]]. In mid-2008, he was nominated as founding president of the [[Institute of Science and Technology Austria]] (ISTA) in [[Maria Gugging]] near [[Vienna]],<ref>{{webarchive |url=https://archive.today/20120713210014/http://orf.at/ticker/294296.html |date=July 13, 2012 |archive-is=20120713210014 |title=ORF.at: I.S.T. Austria: Gehirnforscher Bonhoeffer wird erster Chef |access-date=2022-09-01}}</ref> but announced on July 21, 2008 that he would decline the offered leadership position at the ISTA for personal reasons.<ref>{{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160519070348/http://sciencev1.orf.at/science/news/152085 |archive-is=20160519070348 |title=ORF.at: Elite-Uni: Gehirnforscher Bonhoeffer doch nicht Chef |access-date=2022-09-01}}</ref>

In 2014, Bonhoeffer was appointed to the Board of Governors of the UK [[Wellcome Trust]],<ref name=":6">{{cite web |url=https://wellcome.ac.uk/press-release/professor-bryan-grenfell-and-professor-tobias-bonhoeffer-join-wellcome-trust-board |title=Professor Bryan Grenfell and Professor Tobias Bonhoeffer join the Wellcome Trust Board of Governors |date=7 July 2014 |publisher=Wellcome Trust |access-date=2022-09-01 |language=English}}</ref> where he served as governor until the end of 2021. In 2016, he became a scientific advisor to the [[Chan Zuckerberg Initiative]], founded by [[Mark Zuckerberg]] and his wife [[Priscilla Chan]].<ref name=":7">{{cite web |url=https://www.welt.de/wissenschaft/article159267339/So-will-Mark-Zuckerberg-alle-Krankheiten-besiegen.html |title=So will Mark Zuckerberg alle Krankheiten besiegen |date=10 November 2016 |access-date=2022-09-01 |publisher=Welt.de |language=German}}</ref> In 2017, he was elected chairman of the Scientific Council of the Max Planck Society. 

== Scientific focus ==
Bonhoeffer's work focuses on the cellular foundations of learning and memory as well as on the early postnatal development of the brain. He and his research group were the first to demonstrate the presence of "pinwheels" in the mammalian visual system, using high-resolution imaging techniques.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Bonhoeffer |first1=T |last2=Grinvald |first2=A |title=Iso-orientation domains in cat visual cortex are arranged in pinwheel-like patterns |journal=Nature |volume=353 |issue=6343 |pages=429–431 |date=October 1991 |pmid=1896085 |doi=10.1038/353429a0|bibcode=1991Natur.353..429B |s2cid=4342857 }}</ref> Further research dealt with [[nerve growth factor]]s, in particular [[brain-derived neurotrophic factor]] (BDNF);<ref name=":1">{{cite journal |last1=Korte |first1=M |last2=Carroll |first2=P |last3=Wolf |first3=E |last4=Brem |first4=G |last5=Thoenen |first5=H |last6=Bonhoeffer |first6=T |title=Hippocampal long-term potentiation is impaired in mice lacking brain-derived neurotrophic factor |journal=Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A |volume=92 |issue=19 |pages=8856–8860 |date=September 12, 1995 |pmid=7568031 |pmc=41066 |doi=10.1073/pnas.92.19.8856|bibcode=1995PNAS...92.8856K |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite journal |last1=Korte |first1=M |last2=Griesbeck |first2=O |last3=Gravel |first3=C |last4=Carroll |first4=P |last5=Staiger |first5=V |last6=Thoenen |first6=H |last7=Bonhoeffer |first7=T |title=Virus-mediated gene transfer into hippocampal CA1 region restores long-term potentiation in brain-derived neurotrophic factor mutant mice |journal=Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A |volume=93 |issue=22 |pages=12547–12552 |date=October 29, 1996 |pmid=8901619 |pmc=38029 |doi=10.1073/pnas.93.22.12547|bibcode=1996PNAS...9312547K |doi-access=free }}</ref> the functional strengthening of [[synapse]]s, which is reflected in morphological changes of neurons through the formation of new [[dendritic spine]]s;<ref name=":3">{{cite journal |last1=Engert |first1=F |last2=Bonhoeffer |first2=T |title=Dendritic spine changes associated with hippocampal long-term synaptic plasticity |journal=Nature |volume=399 |issue=6731 |pages=66–70 |date=May 1999 |pmid=10331391 |doi=10.1038/19978|bibcode=1999Natur.399...66E |s2cid=4355911 }}</ref> the targeted degradation of [[protein]]s as a mechanism for the storage of information in the nervous system;<ref name=":4">{{cite journal |last1=Fonseca |first1=R |last2=Vabulas |first2=RM |last3=Hartl |first3=FU |last4=Bonhoeffer |first4=T |last5=Nägerl |first5=UV |title=A balance of protein synthesis and proteasome-dependent degradation determines the maintenance of LTP |journal=Neuron |volume=52 |issue=2 |pages=239–245 |date=October 19, 2006 |pmid=17046687 |doi=10.1016/j.neuron.2006.08.015|doi-access=free }}</ref> and with the process by which many cell contacts that were grown during learning are inactivated but not degraded when they are not used, which should enable much faster relearning.<ref name=":5">{{cite journal |last1=Hofer |first1=SB |last2=Mrsic-Flogel |first2=TD |last3=Bonhoeffer |first3=T |last4=Hübener |first4=M |title=Experience leaves a lasting structural trace in cortical circuits |journal=Nature |volume=457 |issue=7227 |pages=313–317 |date=January 15, 2009 |pmid=19005470 |pmc=6485433 |doi=10.1038/nature07487|bibcode=2009Natur.457..313H }}</ref>

== Important discoveries ==
Bonhoeffer's work led to a number of important scientific discoveries. These include:

* the demonstration of the existence of "pinwheels" in the mammalian visual system by intrinsic optical imaging (Bonhoeffer & Grinvald, Nature 1991)<ref name=":0" />
* the demonstration that [[neurotrophin]]s, in particular [[brain-derived neurotrophic factor]], play an important role in [[synaptic plasticity]] (Korte et al., PNAS 1995 & 1996)<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />
* the observation that the functional strengthening of [[synapse]]s is accompanied by morphological changes in the neuron, specifically by the formation of [[dendritic spine]]s (Engert & Bonhoeffer, Nature 1999)<ref name=":3" />
* the demonstration that hippocampal spines exhibit activity-dependent, bidirectional structural plasticity (Nägerl et al., Neuron 2004)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nägerl |first1=UV |last2=Eberhorn |first2=N |last3=Cambridge |first3=SB |last4=Bonhoeffer |first4=T |title=Bidirectional activity-dependent morphological plasticity in hippocampal neurons |journal=Neuron |volume=44 |issue=5 |pages=759–767 |date=December 2004 |pmid=15572108 |doi=10.1016/j.neuron.2004.11.016|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* the demonstration that long-lasting synaptic plasticity depends on both [[protein]] synthesis and protein degradation (Fonseca et al., Neuron 2006)<ref name=":4" />
* the finding that new synaptic contacts established during a [[learning]] process persist even if the learned information has been [[forgetting|forgotten]]; this facilitates subsequent relearning (Hofer et al., Nature 2009)<ref name=":5" />
* the demonstration that rodents can learn to assign visual stimuli to categories, and that important changes occur in the medial prefrontal cortex during this learning process (Reinert et al., Nature 2021)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Reinert |first1=S |last2=Hübener |first2=M |last3=Bonhoeffer |first3=T |last4=Goltstein |first4=PM |title=Mouse prefrontal cortex represents learned rules for categorization |journal=Nature |volume=593 |issue=7859 |pages=411–417 |date=May 20, 2021 |pmid=33883745 |pmc=8131197 |doi=10.1038/s41586-021-03452-z|bibcode=2021Natur.593..411R }}</ref>
